transcription.original_script:
№ 1
Попово
1877 года
Состоялось въ Посадѣ Сероцкѣ четвертаго (шестнадцатаго
Января, тысяча восемьсотъ семьдесятъ седьмаго года, въ десять ча-
совъ утра. — Явился лично Моисеева Закона Довидъ Сендеръ Шах-
цѣръ, шестидесяти четырехъ лѣтъ отъ роду, въ Деревнѣ Попо-
вѣ жительствующій, въ присутствіи свидѣтелей Моисеева
Закона Файбеша Розенберга сапожника, тридцати девяти лѣтъ
отъ роду и Мортка Фишмана мясника, сорока четырехъ
лѣтъ отъ роду, здѣсь въ Сероцкѣ жительствующихъ, и предъ-
явилъ намъ младенца мужескаго пола, объявляя, что онъ ро-
дился въ Деревнѣ Поповѣ Двадцать седьмаго Декабря (восьмаго
Января, тысяча восемьсотъ семьдесятъ шестаго (седьмаго) го-
да, въ четыре часа утра отъ законной его жены Хава урож-
денной Бухманъ, сорока пяти лѣтъ отъ роду. Младенцу
этому при обрѣзаніи дано имя Анкелъ. Актъ сей объяв-
ляющему и свидѣтелямъ прочитанъ, а затѣмъ объявляю-
щимъ, свидѣтелями, а также нами подписанъ
dawid Solarz    Faibisz Rozenberg
Мортка Фишманъ
Содержащій Акты Гражданскаго Состоянія
transcription.translation: No. 1. Popowo. Year 1877. It took place in the Posad of Serock on the fourth (sixteenth) of January, one thousand eight hundred seventy-seven, at ten o'clock in the morning. There appeared in person Dowid Sender Szachcer, of the Mosaic faith, sixty-four years of age, residing in the village of Popowo, in the presence of the witnesses Fajbisz Rozenberg, of the Mosaic faith, shoemaker, thirty-nine years of age, and Mortka Fiszman, butcher, forty-four years of age, both residing here in Serock, and he presented to us an infant of male sex, declaring that it was born in the village of Popowo on the twenty-seventh of December (the eighth of January), one thousand eight hundred seventy-six (seventy-seven), at four o'clock in the morning, of his lawful wife Chawa née Buchman, forty-five years of age. This infant was given the name Ankiel at the circumcision. This act was read to the declarant and the witnesses, and was thereupon signed by the declarant, by the witnesses, and also by us. dawid Solarz. Faibisz Rozenberg. Mortka Fiszman. Keeper of the Registers of Civil Status.

notes: CONTRADICTS THE BATCH BRIEF. The brief pins target.language = "pl"; the ink on this act is Russian in pre-reform orthography (Cyrillic), not Polish. Recorded as read from the page per the prompt's 'read the page itself' rule.

Consistent with the Napoleonic-formula skill, which places Russian-language registration at roughly 1868-1915; 1877 is inside that window. No Polish-language formula wording appears anywhere on the act.
Pre-reform letters present throughout: ѣ (лѣтъ, Посадѣ, Деревнѣ), і (присутствіи, Состоянія), terminal ъ.
Locative of Посадъ Сероцкъ; matches the brief's town pin, read independently from the ink.

First of two day-words. Crops made at 3.6x, 4.5x, 5x, 7x and 9x over source region (2265,240,530,72); above about 6x the scan's own resolution (roughly 190 dpi for this spread) blurs rather than resolves, so 3.6-5x was the useful range.
Reading rests on a mid-word tall в-loop plus two m-form т's, which favours четвертаго; пятаго retained because the initial letters stay soft.
Cross-check: paired with the second day-word this gives a 12-day Julian/Gregorian gap, correct for 1877, which supports четвертаго/шестнадцатаго over пятаго/шестнадцатаго (an 11-day gap).
Second day-word, parenthesised. The -надцатаго tail is firm; the initial cluster (шест- vs сем-) is not.
The opening parenthesis is inked as a small hooked stroke; the closing parenthesis is not clearly present on this act, the line instead running out into a ruled filler stroke.

Dual dating confirmed physically present: two day-words are visible. Compare act 7 on the 07-10 spread, where the same clerk writes 'одиннадцатаго (Двадцать тре...' in the identical slot, which is what established the parenthesis form for this hand.
Both day-words are physically inked, so the dual date is recorded rather than inferred. Julian-to-Gregorian gap of 12 days is correct for 1877.
Written out in words; also confirmed by the page header '1877 года'.
The word часовъ is split across the line break; excerpt quoted with the break as inked.

Line-break surname split (the register-trap named in the paleography skill): the surname begins at the end of line 3 and continues at the start of line 4. Joined token tested in the same slot; the join itself is secure, the letters are not.

Given names Довидъ Сендеръ are firm. The surname is not: crops at 5.5x and 8x over source (2530,335,260,58) and (1660,383,200,58) leave the second element reading as -цѣръ or -теръ, with the т/ш macron ambiguity from the paleography skill in play.

Cross-check against the signature block, which carries a Latin-script autograph reading 'dawid Sołtarz' (or 'Sotiarz'). The given name agrees with the body text; the surname does not obviously agree with either body candidate, so both are retained rather than one being chosen.
Not silently completed from context, per the Goldfarb-trap rule against calling a surname from its first letters.

Cross-check from act 7 of this register year, whose signature block is the most legible in the group: there the same Latin-script surname shape is unambiguously Solarsz/Solarz. That makes the Soltarz reading given here doubtful, and Solarz is added as a candidate. The Cyrillic body form on this act still does not reconcile with either, so nothing is collapsed.

declarant.relationship_to_child.original_script: отъ законной его жены Хава урож-
notes: The act does not use the word отецъ. Paternity rests on the formula: the declarant предъявилъ намъ младенца and the child is отъ законной его жены, i.e. of his lawful wife. This is the standard declarant-is-father construction, so PROBABLE rather than higher.
No midwife, relative or illegitimacy wording appears in the declarant slot.
Written in words, genitive. Note the tension with the stated maternal age of 45: not impossible, and not adjusted.
Village name split across the line 4/5 break; quoted across the break as inked.
The same name appears three times on this act, at the declarant's residence, the child's birthplace and the margin annotation, and all three agree.
Crops at 6x and 8x over source (2470,383,300,55) and (1500,255,200,90).

Cross-check: act 4 of this register year, on the better-exposed left-hand page of the 03-06 spread, names the same village. There its margin annotation reads Попово at 8x and its body form Поповѣ is unambiguous, both П letters clearly formed. That settles the п/н question that act 1's dimmer ink leaves open, so Popowo is adopted here rather than left forked.
Моисеева Закона = of the Law of Moses; the register's standard confessional tag, applied here to the declarant and carried over to the witnesses.
Same person as the declarant; see declarant.name for the surname reasoning.

Cross-check from act 7 of this register year, whose signature block is the most legible in the group: there the same Latin-script surname shape is unambiguously Solarsz/Solarz. That makes the Soltarz reading given here doubtful, and Solarz is added as a candidate. The Cyrillic body form on this act still does not reconcile with either, so nothing is collapsed.
The declarant slot in this act carries faith, name, age and residence but no trade word, whereas both witness slots in the same act do carry one (сапожника, мясника).
BLANK rather than ABSENT_ON_FORM: the formula plainly has the slot, and this clerk fills it for other people on the same page; here he simply did not.
Inked in the genitive (Файбеша Розенберга). Corroborated by the Latin-script autograph 'Faibisz Rozenberg' in the signature block, read at 5.5x over source (2150,1000,640,60).
сапожникъ is one of the high-frequency trade words for this register series.
Two large д-loops make the -дцати/девяти skeleton clear; the три- versus два- opening is what stays soft. Crop at 6.5x over source (2380,480,410,55).
Read as три- because the opening strokes are small and precede the loop, whereas два- would open on the loop itself.
The residence phrase is plural and governs both witnesses jointly.

Read first from act 1's own ink at 5.5x and 7x over source (1660,522,700,58) and (2000,528,260,52). On this dimmer right-hand page the given name sat between Мошка and Мортка and the surname between Фришмана and Гриншпана; the Cyrillic autograph below was read as Мортка Гриншпанъ.

Revised after reading act 3 of the same register year, on the better-exposed left-hand page of the 03-06 spread, where the same slot reads Мортка Фишмана unambiguously, the ш carrying this clerk's underline diacritic. This is a within-register consistency cross-check of the kind the uncertainty guidance directs, applied to my own reading of another pinned artifact in the same batch, not to any other reader's output.

Three independent points of agreement identify the man as the same person across the two acts: the given name Мортка, the trade мясника, and the stated age of сорока четырехъ. A witness aging zero years within a single register year is expected.
The excerpt is extended through мясника to keep it uniquely locatable in the transcription.
Kept as UNCLEAR rather than promoted, because act 1's own ink does not compel Фишмана on its own and a single reader may not emit CONFIDENT. All three candidate readings are retained.
Age phrase straddles the line 7/8 break; excerpt quoted across the break as inked.
Shared plural residence phrase covering both witnesses.
Crops at 5.5x and 10x over source (2265,858,180,62); 10x is past the scan's real resolution and blurs, so the 5.5x read governs.
The initial capital matches the same clerk's capital А in 'Актъ' two words later on the same line, so the name begins with А.
The medial letter is the к/ц/ш group, which this hand does not separate cleanly. All three onomastically live candidates are retained; none is silently preferred.
No surname is given for the infant, which is normal for this act type.
Stated explicitly in the presentation slot.
Independently corroborated by the naming slot: при обрѣзаніи (at the circumcision) is the boys' naming rite, and the masculine что онъ родился agrees.
Julian side of the birth date. Note the year rolls back to 1876 on the Julian side, which the clerk marks with the paired year-words on line 11.
Gregorian side, parenthesised, split across the line 10/11 break; excerpt quoted across the break as inked.
Gap check: 27 December Julian to 8 January Gregorian is 12 days, correct for the 1800s, and the paired year-words семьдесятъ шестаго (седьмаго) confirm the year crossing.
Both day-words physically inked, and the year is likewise doubled: семьдесятъ шестаго (седьмаго). Derived calendar normalisation is kept in the two separate date observations.
Crop at 6x over source (1800,670,480,55). The birth is in the village, not the posad, consistent with the declarant residing there.

Cross-check: act 4 of this register year, on the better-exposed left-hand page of the 03-06 spread, names the same village. There its margin annotation reads Попово at 8x and its body form Поповѣ is unambiguous, both П letters clearly formed. That settles the п/н question that act 1's dimmer ink leaves open, so Popowo is adopted here rather than left forked.
Left uninflected by the clerk after жены. Read at 5.5x over source (2330,764,460,58).
The née marker урожденной is split across the line 12/13 break; excerpt quoted across the break as inked.

Б and у are firm and the -манъ tail is firm. The single letter between them is a tall loop, which in this hand serves for к, х and ѣ alike, so the middle of the surname is the open question. Crops at 5.5x, 7x and 8x over source (1810,826,260,52).
Flagged as the highest-value field on the act and deliberately left forked rather than resolved to the most familiar surname.
A stated maternal age of 45 at a live birth is high but is what the ink says; not adjusted.
Boys' naming formula, which independently supports the male sex reading.
